questions.answer: Whether the university had the types of classes i was looking for as well as good english speaking professors for their courses in english

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There was a reception at the dorm with 24/7 in-person staffing who could help with any questions. 
You've also had email communication with the international office who you could contact for help with any study related questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Two options for exchange students (International House or SK Global House), i stayed in SK Global House and were very satisfied with my stay

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: SK Global House has a big shared kitchen with cooking utilities as well as shared fridges and freezers for the students to use

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The walls are not that thick and sound travels easily so if you are a light sleeper or sleep earyl you might be disturbed by the other residents at times. There are quiet hours from 12 (night) but not everybody adheres to these. 
There are also both solo and double rooms depending on what you prefer but the solo rooms are more expensive
If you are going on exchange with fellow students you can ask to be roomed with a specific person
There are specific rules for dorm living you need to keep to or you might be kicked out if you break too amny of them

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are two periods of registration. If you do not get all the classes you want or are put on a wait list during the first period you can get the classes you want in the second period or you can get the professor to sign a permission slip stating they will allow you in the class after you arrive at the university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mail was available to ask questions or get help with registration. You could also go to the international offfie on campus and geo in-person help as well

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i was 100% successful in getting my classes but not in one go. I got some during the first and seconf round of registration and the rest through permission from the individual professor.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look up classes from the course list for previous semesters to see which ones you would like to take and the level of difficulty. Write down course codes and make sure they dont overlap time-wise. List them in priority of importance and want as you need to but in number of points for each during the registration.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy for me as i have already gone on exchange before but can be difficult for first timers as the culture is very different from home

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: engange with them and try to speak at bit of their language if you can, they want to socialize but are often embarassed because if their lack of english

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Plan as much as you can in advance it will help you in the long run
apply for any scholarships you can outside of your university it can help with costs
save up as soon as possible as there are a certain amount if lump sum payments you need to make
